title: Successive-quotient inclusion of internal bar cochains
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring, $F$ an internal-function presentation, $J$ a profinite group and $B$ a given bar diagram [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. The cochain and evaluation conventions are [def-sfb-internal-cochain-coordinate-data]. There are internal module maps $i_M^n:C_B^n(M)\to F(J^{n+1},M)$, natural in every equivariant coefficient map, whose evaluation at a tuple $x$ on every profinite slice is $x_0c(x_0^{-1}x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n)$. These maps are sectionwise injective, their image is exactly the homogeneous sections on the whole slice, and $i_M^{n+1}d_B$ evaluates as the alternating deletion of $i_M^nc$. Equivalently, the structure BarHomogeneousInclusion F J B is inhabited. No restriction between groups, coordinate isomorphism or derived statement is asserted.

proof.text: Construct the displayed map on natural evaluation families using the evaluation equivalence. The restriction laws for evaluation and the action make it natural in the test object. Addition and scalar compatibility make it linear. Lift these maps through the section-module equivalence. Equivariance of coefficient maps gives naturality in M.

proof.text: Simultaneous left multiplication cancels in successive quotients and acts through x_0, so the image is homogeneous. Evaluation on prefix tuples is a left inverse, since consecutive prefix quotients recover g, proving injectivity. For any homogeneous family take its prefix evaluation as the inverse section. The cumulative products of successive quotients are x_0^{-1}x_i, and homogeneity recovers the original family after acting by x_0. This proves the image equality.

proof.text: Apply the inhomogeneous face formulas. The action face multiplies x_0 by x_0^{-1}x_1 and becomes deletion of x_0; interior faces multiply two consecutive quotients and become deletion of the intermediate x_i; the final face omits the final quotient. Addition and integer scalar multiplication commute with evaluation, so the alternating sum is exactly deletion with its signs. In degree zero this is x_1c-x_0c, as required.
